items.item_text: Upholds Kaiser Permanentes Policies and Procedures, Principles of Responsibilities and applicable state, federal and local laws.

Customer Service: Is responsive to the needs of others by maintaining a professional behavior toward members and coworkers and creating a positive image for the department, as demonstrated by: Willingness to take the initiative to resolve member issues. Handling a high number of member contacts. Dealing with customer complaints in a positive way. Providing compassionate service. Treating coworkers with respect and appreciation. Fostering teamwork and thinking positively. Identifies the impact of cultural diversity and lifestyle choices on patient condition and makes accommodations for such differences. Demonstrates competence in the operation of dedicated and complex mammography equipment in a patient care setting for the purposes of obtaining definitive diagnosis for positive findings on a mammogram. Consistently selects correct technical factors relative to the requirements of the study and the patients age, body habitus and pathology. Consistently selects other equipment settings/parameters (e.g. locks on equipment and tables, tube placement, control panel settings, etc.) appropriately. Consistently processes radiographic images properly, utilizing automated equipment. Critiques images and makes necessary adjustments in technical factors, patient positioning, etc. Uses proper sterile technique and/or proper infection control technique. Consistently operates imaging computer properly and in accordance with department protocols. Conducts a patient interview to attain full understanding of procedure and ultimately obtaining consent of the patient. Demonstrates knowledge of, and consistently uses ancillary equipment (e.g. catheters, guidewires, etc.) properly. Demonstrates competence in the positioning of patients for mammography imaging.
2. Performs all the duties/responsibilities enumerated in the Job Description for Mammography Technologist I. In addition, Mammography Technologists II perform the following :

Operates complex invasive mammographic unit to include but not limited to stereotactic breast biopsy equipment, ductogram, cyst aspiration, and needle localization in a patient care setting for the purposes of obtaining definitive diagnosis for positive findings on a mammogram.

Assists with orientation and training of students and other radiologic technologists in stereotactic biopsy procedures, equipment and techniques. Positions patients for mammography images. Accurately positions patients taking into consideration body habitus and location of lesion(s) and calcification(s). Masters precise positioning techniques involved with stereotactic procedures.
Maintains a comprehensive knowledge of, and ability to perform, required mammography Q.C. for stereotactic breast biopsy equipment according to the requirements of the State of California and MQSA.
Performs delicate and accurate calibration of stereotactic breast biopsy equipment.
Exercises clinical judgment within scope of practice.
Consults with the radiologist or other clinician for purposes of clarifying orders or questionable images, tissue, structures.
Documents stereotactic biopsy and other clinical activities in timely, comprehensive and accurate manner.
Completes and initials the standard consultation form and/or the Radiology Processing Record accurately and immediately following each procedure.
Accurately documents all pertinent information regarding stereotactic breast biopsy procedures according to required standards of MQSA, ACR, HCFA, State of California, FDA.
ORGANIZATIONAL RULES, POLICIES AND PROCEDURES
Observes all applicable Regional, Medical Center and Departmental policies and procedures.
QUALITY OF SERVICE
Maintains established departmental, institutional and organizational standards of professional behavior established to enhance quality of member/patient service.
COMMUNICATION
Communicates clearly, effectively and appropriately at all times.
PROFESSIONAL MATURITY
Exhibits professional maturity in all interactions with patients and staff.
Strives to maintain good working relationships and rapport with patients and members of other departments involved to provide continuity of care.
PRODUCTIVITY
Strives to meet productivity norms within the department or Region.
EQUIPMENT, SUPPLIES AND WORK AREA

Maintains equipment, supplies and work area in accordance with department guidelines. Keeps equipment and work area clean at all times, including detailed cleaning of equipment and instruments. Handles equipment with care to avoid damage. Reports quality control issues to supervisor and/or appropriate service personnel.
May perform other duties as assigned within the Diagnostic Imaging Department.
Minimum of two years experience as a Mammography staff technologist within the last two years.
Invasive Breast procedures within the last 2 years.
Knowledge of sterile field preparation.
Screening & Diagnostic Breast Imaging experience within the past 12 months.
Certified Radiologic Technologist - Mammography Certificate (California)
Radiologic Technologist Certificate (California)
American Registry of Radiologic Technologists Certificate - Mammography Technologist within 3 months of hire from American Registry of Radiologic Technologists
Basic Life Support within 3 months of hire
Radiologic Technologist Certification within 3 months of hire from American Registry of Radiologic Technologists

Ability to demonstrate and apply knowledge, Principles and practices of radiologic, mammographic techniques, digital mammography, invasive breast procedures to include stereotactic breast biopsies, breast structures, anatomy, composition and pathology.
Demonstrated ability to perform Quality control/Assurance functions required for mammography as specified by State of California and Mammography Quality Standards Act.
This position is to support Mammography Services at the Zion Medical Center. Stereotactic, Breast Localizations, Diagnostic Mammo, Screening Mammo
Scheduled work hours per week will be 20-32.
